official.deadline_note: AfDB publishes no central call opening or closing date. Applications go only through the partner universities, and AfDB's own List of Universities page publishes each partner's intake and application window, e.g. Hiroshima University (April intake: preliminary survey Oct 18-29, application period Nov 8-19), The University of Tokyo (Schedule B application period mid November), Sophia University (September intake: web entry mid March to early April, application mid April) and Ritsumeikan Asia Pacific University (April enrollment deadline October; September enrollment April).
official.application_cycle: Annual; timed to the admissions cycles of the JADS partner universities
official.status_note: The AfDB programme pages carry no round-specific banner; the live application windows are those of the individual partner universities as published on the List of Universities page.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Published: 'Tuition fee coverage for the duration of the study program (24 months).'
benefits: Tuition fee coverage for the duration of the study program (24 months)
Monthly living stipend for the duration of the study program (24 months)
Air travel from the home country to the host university at the start of the study program and back home at the end of the scholarship period
Health insurance, usually obtained through the university
Additional six (6) months for advance preparatory study or internships after graduation
For scholars engaged in research, a special grant may be available for research and thesis preparation
eligibility: Minimum of a Bachelor's degree or its equivalent in energy, agriculture, health, environmental sustainability, engineering studies or related areas, with excellent academic records, relevant professional experience and a history of supporting their countries' development efforts
At least 1 year of paid employment in the home country or in other African countries after receiving the Bachelor's degree within the past 3 years
35 years old or younger, and in good health
Must gain admission to an approved master's degree course at a Japanese or African partner university - application for admission is done directly through the partner universities
Must be a citizen of one of the African Development Bank's regional member countries

Must not be enrolled in another graduate degree program, and must not be an Executive Director, alternate or staff member of the African Development Bank Group or a close relative of the aforementioned
requirements: All applications should go through the partner universities; no separate application to the African Development Bank is necessary
Only candidates who have been offered admission and endorsed by the university will be considered for the JADS Program
Admission by a JADS partner university does not mean the candidate has been accepted for scholarship support

Candidates should prepare: a current curriculum vitae, proof of employment for each record of employment since earning a Bachelor's degree, a certified copy of the certificate of the most advanced university degree earned, two professional references, and a research plan and proposal
documents: Proof of employment for each record of employment since earning a Bachelor's degree
Certified copy of the certificate of the most advanced university degree earned
coverage: Tuition fee coverage for the duration of the study program (24 months)
Monthly living stipend for the duration of the study program (24 months)
Air travel from the home country to the host university at the start of the study program and back home at the end of the scholarship period
Health insurance, usually obtained through the university
Additional six (6) months for advance preparatory study or internships after graduation
application_method: Read the information posted on the JADS website and review the eligibility criteria carefully
Request information, application forms and procedures from the chosen JADS partner university using the contacts published on the List of Universities page
Complete and submit the application for admission to the partner university
The university evaluates and selects applicants and issues provisional offer letters, then sends the selected list to the African Development Bank for evaluation by the Program Implementation Unit
official.application_route: Apply for admission directly to a JADS partner university; the university endorses selected candidates to the African Development Bank - there is no separate application to the Bank.
official.citizenship_residency: Must be a citizen of one of the African Development Bank's regional member countries.
official.international_eligibility: The programme is designed for nationals of African Development Bank regional member countries studying at approved courses at Japanese or African partner universities.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Master's-level study in energy, agriculture, health, environmental sustainability and engineering or related areas, at an approved course of a JADS partner university.
official.research_requirement: Candidates are asked to prepare a research plan and proposal as part of the application file.
official.duration: Two years; 'the scholarship only covers the duration of the graduate program or two years, whichever is less.'
official.description: The Japan Africa Dream Scholarship (JADS) is a capacity building programme of the African Development Bank and the Government of Japan that offers high-achieving African students a two-year scholarship to pursue post-graduate studies at master's level in energy, agriculture, health, environmental sustainability and engineering. Scholars are expected to return to their home countries and contribute to national and continental socio-economic development using the newly acquired knowledge and skills.
official.program_type: Multilateral scholarship programme (African Development Bank and the Government of Japan)
official.english_requirement: AfDB's published preparation guidance says: 'Take TOEFL iBT, TOEC test for English proficiency.' No minimum score, test-sitting date rule or accepted validity period is published.

verification.notes: Read the awarding body's own JADS programme, eligibility, preparation and list-of-universities pages on afdb.org on 2026-10-10; the coverage list, exclusions, eligibility criteria and partner-university windows are confirmed as published. AfDB publishes no stipend figure and no central deadline anywhere on its JADS pages.

applicant_utility.summary: JADS is not applied for directly: you first secure admission to an approved master's course at a Japanese or African partner university, and only university-endorsed candidates reach the Bank's evaluation. AfDB never publishes a stipend figure, so the monthly living allowance has to be confirmed with your chosen university and the JADS Secretariat. The money covers tuition for 24 months, a monthly living stipend, return air travel and health insurance, but the published exclusion list (family costs, extra-curricular courses, supplementary materials, field trips, workshops and computers) means you still carry real incidentals.
applicant_utility.best_fit: African Development Bank member-country citizens aged 35 or under with a relevant bachelor's degree, an excellent academic record and at least one year of paid post-degree employment earned within the past three years.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you are a citizen of an AfDB regional member country, 35 or younger, and not already enrolled in another graduate programme
Check the approved courses on AfDB's List of Universities page and pick a partner university whose intake window you can actually meet
Secure the university admission first - applications go through the partner university, never to the Bank
Assemble proof of employment for every position held since your bachelor's degree, a certified copy of your highest degree certificate, and two professional references
Write the research plan and proposal, and take the TOEFL iBT / TOEIC English test that AfDB's preparation page asks for
common_rejection_risks: Assuming a university admission offer is a scholarship award - AfDB states admission alone does not mean scholarship support
Having no paid employment within three years of the bachelor's degree, or employment outside the home country or other African countries
Holding another graduate enrolment, which makes you ineligible
Applying to a course that is not on the partner university's approved list
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Visa application costs, family support, extra-curricular courses, language training outside the programme, supplementary materials, field trips, workshops, seminars and equipment such as computers are all on AfDB's published 'does not cover' list.
document_audit: Employment proof is required for each record of employment since the bachelor's degree, not just the current job
The degree certificate must be a certified copy of the most advanced university degree earned
Two professional references must be identified by the applicant before the university's own deadline, which runs earlier than any scholarship decision
alerts: AfDB warns finalists and awardees not to take any action with respect to current employment until the Bank confirms the award
The JADS stipend may be withdrawn completely or partially if the programme finds evidence of other sources of support - declare any other funding

Each partner university runs its own admissions calendar (for example Hiroshima University's April intake has an October preliminary survey and November application period), so the effective deadline is the university's, months before any Bank decision
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Apply for admission at a JADS partner university; the university screens and shortlists, then sends the selected candidates to the African Development Bank, whose Program Implementation Unit evaluates the files and contacts successful candidates directly.
